one_month_reasoning: Q3 2026 results are expected Thu Oct 22 after the close (aggregator estimate, not yet confirmed by Intel; ~85-90% likely inside the window) [22]. Guide was $15.8-16.8B revenue / $0.38 EPS [1]. Value-chain read-through into the print is positive: server CPU list prices up 10-20% since March with a further 8-10% signalled for 2H26 and a 12% flagship Xeon hike in July [26,27,9], distributors filling ~40% of backlog [9], and Micron's FQ4 ($54.2B, +379% y/y, Oct 1) confirming AI-server demand [32]. Offsets: IDC sees Q4 PC units -20% y/y on memory costs [33,8], which threatens the Q4 client guide; the company lock-up ends with the Q3 print so a new raise becomes possible (none planned or filed) [23]; and the supervisor's own check found 8 of the last 11 next-day earnings reactions negative with ~11% mean absolute move. Because that base rate is verified and the stock ran +34% in September into ~58x FY27 EPS, I move my median from ~$120.5 (round 1) to ~$119, just below spot, with sigma ~20% for the month (close to 76%/3.5 = 22%, slightly lower because part of the 1-year vol came from deal-headline jumps). A 14A customer announcement could land in the window (PDK 0.9 due October [30]) and is the main right-tail risk; I do not try to time it.

fair_value.method: 50/50 blend of (a) P/E: 2028E EPS $2.73 (prior $2.80 less ~2.6% escrow-share dilution) x 36x = $98 and (b) SOTP: Products 2027E NOPAT $19B x 20x = $380B + foundry option $140B (cut from $200B) + stakes $9.4B + net cash $1.8B - NCI $15.6B = $515.6B over 5.54B fully counted shares = $93. Blend ~$96, about 20% below the $120 price.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: 2028E non-GAAP EPS $2.73 x 36x forward multiple (what the market pays in Oct 2027 for 2028 earnings)

inputs_detail.derivation: 2027 consensus $2.06 grown ~35% to $2.80 (server x86 units +20% y/y and 10-20% list-price increases [4,9,10,26,27]; AMD's +70% server CPU guide shows TAM expansion Intel shares at a lower rate [12]; 18A yields reaching industry standard in 2027 [18]), then cut ~2.6% for the 143M DoC escrow shares that release as Secure Enclave disbursements arrive [23].
Between Nvidia ~25x and AMD ~40x forward P/E [3]; Intel grows slower than both but carries foundry optionality; current ~58-63x on depressed earnings should compress as EPS ramps.

methods.name: SOTP
methods.inputs: Products NOPAT $19B x 20x = $380B; foundry option $140B; stakes $9.4B; net cash $1.8B; less NCI $15.6B; 5.54B fully counted shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Q2 op income annualized ~$19.3B, +12% for 2027 (DCAI pricing/shortage [4,26] offset by client unit pressure from memory costs, IDC Q4 PC -20% y/y [6,8,33]) = ~$21.6B, taxed ~12% (11% guided non-GAAP rate [1]) = ~$19B.
Substack framework uses 17x bear / 22-25x base [2]; 20x given continued x86 share loss to AMD and Arm (Arm 13.6% of servers) [4].

Cut from $200B. Dropped the X-relayed KeyBanc customer list entirely and treat Apple 18A-P/M7 as unconfirmed (reported by Kuo/WSJ/trade press, not announced by either company [29]). External foundry revenue is $293M/qtr [1]. I stay somewhat above the $110-120B the supervisor favours because the chain evidence is more than talk: 18A-P is in risk production [28], Microsoft Maia 2 on 18A/18A-P [16], Fortinet on Intel 4 [31], two prospective 14A customers evaluating test chips with decisions expected 2H26-1H27 [30], and 14A risk production H2 2027 / HVM 2028 reaffirmed [25,34]. Roughly: ~50% odds of a binding 14A anchor within 12 months x ~$250B success value (Substack base $265-300B [2]) plus ~$15B for existing 18A/Intel 4 external work.
Pro forma cash + ST investments ~$52.3B (incl. $22.62B net offering proceeds with greenshoe) less $50.5B debt [23,24]; before H2 2026 burn.

5,285M basic after full greenshoe + ~119M unvested RSUs/PSUs = ~5.40B diluted, + 143M escrowed DoC shares likely released within the horizon [23,24]; 241M contingent warrants excluded (only if foundry ownership < 51%).

bear.story: 14A decisions slip or go to TSMC/Samsung and Apple 18A-P stays unconfirmed/small; server CPU pricing normalises in 2027 as supply grows while AMD/Arm keep taking share [4,5]; memory-driven PC decline extends into 2027 [6,8,33]; a post-lock-up equity raise adds dilution [23]. Market values Intel as a ~17x products company with near-zero foundry option after NCI (~$60-68/share).

base.story: Server CPU shortage and pricing persist into 2027 [9,26,27]; 18A yields normalise [18]; EPS tracks ~$2+ for 2027; one 14A or 18A-P commitment announced but foundry still loss-making; multiple compresses as EPS grows, leaving the stock somewhat below today.

bull.story: Apple M7 on 18A-P confirmed and shipping from late 2027 [29], a named 14A anchor (Apple/Nvidia/Microsoft-class) signs a capacity reservation [30], agentic-AI CPU TAM step-up [12,13] lets DCAI grow 40%+ despite share loss; market values the foundry as a credible TSMC second source.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$70 (-42%) the market is pricing essentially zero foundry option: Products at 20x ($380B) plus stakes and net cash, less the $15.6B NCI, is ~$68/share on 5.54B shares [23]. It is also ~26% below the $95 August offering price and well under the July 2026 low near $82. Getting there most likely means a fundamental failure (14A anchor customers walk, 18A/18A-P yield problems, or server pricing reversing while share loss accelerates) rather than ordinary 70%-vol noise.

reasoning: Round 2 keeps my industry-lane view but corrects the balance-sheet inputs and the foundry value per the supervisor. Facts adopted: greenshoe exercised ($23B gross, 242.1M shares; 5,285M basic, ~5.40B diluted plus 143M escrow) [23,24]; $15.6B NCI must be deducted [23]; Apple deal remains unconfirmed [29]; KeyBanc customer list via X discounted and no longer used. Follow-up lane checks: TrendForce confirms server CPU prices +10-20% since March with more hikes signalled and a 12% flagship Xeon increase [26,27]; Micron's Oct 1 FQ4 ($54.2B) confirms AI-server demand but also memory-cost pressure on PCs, where IDC sees Q4 units -20% y/y [32,33]; on foundry, 18A-P is in risk production [28], PDK 0.9 is due in October with two prospective 14A customers evaluating test chips [30], but no anchor is named. Valuation: P/E $98 and SOTP $93 blend to ~$96 (from $105), about 20% below spot at ~58x FY27 EPS; consensus PT ~$116 is evidence, not the answer. I keep the foundry option at $140B, above the supervisor-favoured $110-120B, because the chain evidence (risk production, Maia 2, Fortinet, imminent PDK, reaffirmed 14A schedule) gives roughly even odds of an anchor within the horizon. Distribution: lognormal-like with median ~$111 (down from ~$115: lower fair value, offset by momentum, pricing power and a binary foundry catalyst) and sigma ~0.58, with a slightly fatter lower tail for dilution/raise risk and 5% above $300 for the foundry binary. Scenarios bear $62/27%, base $110/45%, bull $180/28% give a mean ~$117. 1-month median nudged to ~$119 on the verified negative earnings-reaction base rate. Research limited to ~6 extra queries; some trade pages (Tom's Hardware body text) were not fully fetchable; no option data or priors consulted.
